entry.title: Causal clustering: design of cluster experiments under network interference
entry.summary: A new framework for designing cluster experiments to estimate global treatment effects in the presence of network spillovers. The authors formulate the optimal clustering choice as a penalized min-cut optimization problem to minimize worst-case mean-squared error, addressing the bias-variance trade-off in network experiments.
entry.relevance: Directly addresses a key challenge in causal inference and AI evaluation on networked data, which is core to our research interests in multi-agent systems and reliable evaluation.
